children: NatWest Group's share price decline is overdone, but the bank's net interest margin expansion will be muted, Berenberg's Michael Christodoulou writes. The British bank's new guidance forecasts a broadly stable net interest margin for both the fourth quarter and for 2027. This seems to reflect the bank's plan to increase business volumes, coupled with lower margins, Berenberg writes. As a result, net interest income will continue to grow but margin expansion will be limited, the analyst says. Berenberg cuts its outer-year earnings per share estimates by between 5% and 7% to reflect NatWest's margin outlook and the higher U.K. surcharge tax rate. Despite this, Berenberg says the stock is still cheap. Shares closed 8.8% lower at 579.60 pence on Friday. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
